transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Orchid Eng Lead), Maya Patel (Orchid Head ML), Sam Rivera (CTO), Drew Kim (SRE)
---
Summary:
Quick migration demo and console walkthrough focused on mapping Orchid's OpenAI/Together-based endpoints to Redwood API and Dedicated options. We covered parity gaps (tokens, streaming, function calling), console observability, and a proposed pilot with dedicated capacity to validate latency and cost for genomics inference workloads. Several security and network questions (VPC, KMS, SOC2) surfaced; next steps agreed (benchmarks, pricing, security pack).

Topics covered:
- High-level parity mapping: model equivalents and behavioral testing
- Console tour: routing, rollouts, token-level cost analytics
- Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching, quantization, KV/prefix caching
- Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency
- Pilot plan and timeline

Auto action items (captured above)
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the Orchid account, with Priya from our SE team. we want to walk through the parity mapping and then hop into the console and a small optimize demo.
[00:18] Jordan: Great thanks, Alex. quick context, we run a mixture of OpenAI endpoints for chat and a couple of Together models for internal batch inferences. main SLOs are sub-200ms 99p for short prompts, and cost per call needs to stay under our current baseline, otherwise finance will kill the project.
[00:34] Priya: Got it. and is that latency target for online low-token calls or longer sequence summarization?
[00:40] Maya: Mostly short, interactive annotations — 20 to 80 tokens typically, but we also have nightly batch jobs for variant calling that hit much longer seqs.
[00:50] Alex: Ok that helps, so today we'll show an example map from gpt-4o-ish behaviour to our open models plus show Dedicated capacity where you can get stability on 99p latency. also we'll highlight optimizations — KV cache, batching, quantize profiles.
[01:05] Sam: quick Q on data residency: some of our patient-adjacent notes need to stay in eu-west only. can you host in our VPC or do you do region pinning on Hosted?
[01:15] Priya: we do both — Hosted can pin regionally for many workloads; for strict residency and egress controls Dedicated or Redwood Private (on-prem / VPC) is typical. we support customer KMS integrations for key control.
[01:28] Drew: if we go Dedicated, what's the network topology? like do we need a dedicated vpn, or can we peer?
[01:35] Priya: both options. we can do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your infra. for strict air-gapped we also offer an appliance-based Private deploy but that's a longer engagement.
[01:48] Jordan: and SSO/SAML for internal access? we need RBAC and audit logs for every token.
[01:54] Alex: yes SOC2 + SAML SSO + granular RBAC and audit logs. we'll share the security pack.
[02:04] Priya: jumping to parity: when you say Together models, can you remind us which exact endpoints or model names? sometimes together names are internal.
[02:12] Maya: we used together/mosaic-13b for a lot of our batch and a tuned gpt-4-like for chat via OpenAI.
[02:20] Priya: ok. so two lanes: smallish 13B open model equivalents and a higher quality chat model. our mapping often uses quantized 13B variants and our ensemble for higher quality. important to run behavioral evals because tokenization and sampling diffs show up.
[02:35] Jordan: that was our concern — hallucination rates differ, plus function calling parity for structured output. how do you handle functioncall behavior?
[02:44] Alex: Redwood API supports function-calling and structured output. there are subtle differences — e.g. some models' json proposals differ, recommended step is to lock model version and run your prompt set through both to validate. we have eval tooling in Console to compare side-by-side.
[03:00] Priya: showing the Console now — (screen share) dashboard, per-route latency, token cost heatmap. you can see here cost per route and token-level breakdown, so you can trace expensive prompts.
[03:18] Maya: i like the token breakdown, can it highlight which prompts caused regressions over time?
[03:24] Priya: yes, we have a regressions tab where you attach a prompt set and it flags quality drift tied to model changes or quantization.
[03:30] Alex: also Optimize gives quantize and batching suggestions. for example, if your seq length distribution is small, we recommend a micro-batching policy that trades a few ms for 20-30% cost savings.
[03:45] Drew: micro-batching = added latency. do we risk missing the 200ms 99p?
[03:50] Priya: it's configurable. you can set latency SLOs per route. the runtime will balance batch depth with SLOs; for interactive routes you'll typically keep batch size low and rely on KV caching for repeat prefixes.
[04:03] Jordan: how about streaming — we rely on streaming for live annotations so clients can render partial tokens. does Redwood stream?
[04:10] Alex: yes streaming supported, function calling streaming as well. note: behavior may differ slightly with model variants — we'll show a demo of a streamed chat with function call.
[04:20] Priya: (shares example) here's a streamed response from a Redwood hosted model vs a quantized local Dedicated model — you can see token cadence differences, but UX is intact.
[04:36] Maya: curious about cost delta: for our annotated calls at scale, is it cheaper to use hosted variable usage or reserve Dedicated?
[04:42] Alex: we did a quick TCO earlier — for steady usage, Dedicated with reserved capacity plus auto-burst gives predictable unit costs and often lowers per-token spend by ~30-50% vs hosted. hosted is better for spiky or early-stage. we'll send a tailored worksheet.
[04:58] Sam: what's the commitment on Dedicated? can we do a 3-month pilot?
[05:04] Priya: yes pilots are common — we can spin up reserved capacity for a short pilot and meter it. contracts are flexible.
[05:12] Jordan: on the technical side, for long sequences (variant calling) how well do you maintain kv caches for long context?
[05:21] Priya: our runtime supports large KV cache management and we have a seq-length-aware kernel selection — for very long sequences we recommend a chunked approach plus prefix caching. we'll run a specific benchmark with your variant-calling workload.
[05:35] Maya: ok great. can we talk about evals — I need to see precision/recall-ish metrics on our prompts, not just token-level cost?
[05:44] Alex: Console's evals allow you to run your labeled prompt set and produce metrics (accuracy, best-of, hallucination flags). we can surface per-model metrics and highlight regression alerts.
[05:55] Jordan: any big gotchas migrating from OpenAI's function calling?
[06:01] Priya: structure is the same pattern but small differences in the json encoding of returns and the model's propensity to close objects. systematic test will find these and we provide a compatibility shim if needed.
[06:12] Sam: network egress — if we use Hosted but route to eu-west, will data cross borders? we need proof of no-cross-border egress for certain datasets.
[06:22] Alex: for strict no-cross-border you should use Dedicated in the region or Redwood Private. Hosted regional pinning helps but doesn't meet all strict legal gates. we'll include the data residency doc.
[06:33] Priya: jumping back to the console — here's rollout controls. you can do canaries, A/B, auto-fallback to a cheaper model if the primary fails SLO. this is used a lot when customers want graceful degradation.
[06:48] Maya: auto-fallback — would that change semantics of the output? how do we handle downstream validation?
[06:54] Alex: fallback can be to a model variant with different cost/latency; Console flags those calls and you can set guardrails to reject if output fails a structural validation. you get traceability in the logs.
[07:06] Drew: SRE question — logs/trace retention, where do logs live and who can access?
[07:12] Priya: logs are stored in the customer account; access is via RBAC and SSO. for Dedicated we can integrate with your SIEM/export. retention is configurable.
[07:22] Jordan: ok, let's walk through a short parity-run. Priya: I'll run a small adapted prompt we got from Maya and show the Redwood hosted vs a quantized Dedicated run.
[07:33] Priya: (runs prompt) Hosted Redwood model returns in ~90ms, tokens 42, cost x; Dedicated quantized run returns in ~120ms but cost per-token is ~40% lower. note tokenization differences slightly change token counts.
[07:50] Maya: hmm the Dedicated output truncated a list; might be a sampling / stopping token difference. this is the sort of drift we worried about.
[07:58] Priya: yes that's why we recommend locking model + verification tests. we can tune generation params and sampling to better match behavior.
[08:08] Alex: for the pilot we propose: 1) run your 200 eval prompts across hosted and Dedicated quantized variants; 2) run nightly batch long-sequence tests; 3) review quality metrics and choose a final mapping.
[08:22] Jordan: timeline question — procurement wants vendor decision by end of May. that gives us about 6 weeks. can you commit to deliverables in that window?
[08:31] Alex: yes. benchmark + pricing + security docs within two weeks, then a result review week after — should be fine.
[08:38] Sam: any limitations on model families — we use some community tuned models, do you accept custom model imports?
[08:45] Priya: yes we can onboard model artifacts; for some model formats we need conversion. also if you bring a custom model we can run it in Dedicated with private storage for weights and support quantization.
[08:57] Drew: last infra Q — do you support ephemeral keys and tokenization rotation? we need short-lived credentials for ops.
[09:03] Alex: yes short-lived tokens + KMS integration for keys.
[09:08] Priya: one more demo bit — Optimize suggestions: here it recommends a quantize profile and a batching policy that would save ~28% cost with <10ms avg added latency for our sample distribution.
[09:22] Maya: sounds promising. will need to see the hallucination tradeoffs.
[09:27] Alex: we'll include a column in the benchmark sheet for quality delta so you can see cost vs quality tradeoff.
[09:33] Jordan: ok good. can you also show how we can do A/B with our telemetry hooking? we push traces to datadog.
[09:40] Priya: yep we have tracing hooks and can export to datadog or splunk. you can instrument per-route and tag tokens tied to user ids.
[09:50] Sam: procurement will ask about support SLAs for Dedicated. what's your standard?
[09:57] Alex: Dedicated comes with an SLA tiering option — 99.9 uptime for reserved pools, with phone support for high tiers. we'll put the SLA doc in the security pack.
[10:06] Jordan: cool, any final blockers from your side?
[10:10] Maya: security wants to see SOC2 type 2 and key handling detail; i'll share the exact control list.
[10:16] Alex: we'll send the SOC2 report and a KMS integration guide.
[10:20] Drew: ok i'll compile the VPC and fw rules and send them.
[10:24] Alex: perfect. recap then — we'll share pricing/TCO, spin up ephemeral bench Dedicated pool, run the 200 prompt eval and the long-seq batch, and reconvene to review results.
[10:35] Jordan: thanks all. schedule the follow-up and we'll loop in procurement and security.
[10:40] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and the proposed times.

(End of meeting)
